svg.text: Symmetric vs. anti-symmetric coupling between two layers
Two grids of oscillators, stacked one on the other, each coupled to the oscillator in the same position in the other grid.
The layers lock together and peak as one.
Still locked — but half a cycle apart.
A chases B; B flees A. The waves never repeat.
direction of coupling; the sign in the circle is its coefficient
The point: both-positive and both-negative are the same kind of situation — the layers are symmetric, and they synchronise. Two clocks in anti-phase are still the
same clock, just pointing 180° apart. It is the asymmetric case that is a recipe for chaos: one layer is trying to imitate the other while the other is trying to differ
from it, and the system settles into a strange attractor whose waves never repeat.
